correctness.rationale: Lucas parity for binomial(w,q−1) where q=2^j gives a phase -1 precisely for total weight ≡q−1 (mod q), so the n-qubit hypergraph amplitude matrix is constant on Hamming-weight residue classes. Both subsystem sizes ≥q−1 realize all residues. Compression by normalized residue superpositions gives T=D_m(11ᵀ−2R)D_b, and invertible diagonals leave rank determined by reversal permutation R. Direct multiplication (11ᵀ−2R)(11ᵀ−2R)ᵀ=4I+(q−4)11ᵀ gives eigenvalues (q−2)^2 once and 4 (q−1)-fold; for q≥8 rank is q. Fourier root-of-unity filter makes each residue probability tend to 1/q as both blocks grow at fixed q. Hence exact limiting spectrum {(1−2/q)^2,4/q² [q−1 times]}, and purity/entropy S_q=O(log q/q)→0 as the second limit q→∞. Independent direct diagonalization of a 128×128 computational-basis amplitude matrix for q=8,m=b=7 matched compressed spectrum; independent q=8,16,32 reversal eigenvalues verified. The proof establishes all q, not the finite checks.

value.rationale: For physically natural complete-uniform hypergraph states the theorem computes every nonzero bipartite eigenvalue using a small cyclic matrix rather than an exponentially large amplitude matrix. It sharply separates Schmidt rank, which grows unbounded, from operational von Neumann entropy, which vanishes after the stated sequential limit; this is a motivated many-body entanglement phenomenon rather than an arbitrary parameter substitution.
